role_and_message.evidence: The M figure still compares RBox, HBox and point supervision as three annotation paradigms and explains point-label cost/efficiency motivation.

panel_and_object_coverage.evidence: All source annotation photographs, the HBox special-label mosaic, three corresponding RBox result photographs and all method lists are retained.

labels_math_and_numbers.evidence: Prices $86/1k, $63/1k, $42/1k and method names including PointOBB, H2RBox/H2RBox-v2, OAOD and KCR match the source.

connections_and_direction.evidence: The original row-to-corresponding-result relations are reoriented into three columns with downward arrows to the same result images.

visual_encodings.evidence: Original green annotation boxes/points and red result boxes remain exact. Column colors group the three paradigms; cost/speed wording preserves the original contrast.

examples_and_data.evidence: Seven complete original annotation/result regions independently match native-resolution source pixels, including all detection-box corners and points.

unsupported_additions.evidence: No new measured comparison is added. The three price and high/low cost-speed statements are inherited from the original figure.

complete_visible_content.evidence: All labels, three columns and complete result photographs are visible; the HBox Labeled Data and Special Labeled Data text was additionally inspected enlarged.

remaining_limitations: Original data resolution and notation are retained; perceived quality is left to independent blind scoring.
caption:
Figure 1. The main paradigmatic types of existing oriented ob-
ject detection. Existing methods are primarily divided into rotated
boxes (RBox)-supervised, horizontal boxes (HBox)-supervised,
and Point-supervised approaches. Compared to RBox and HBox
labels, point labels have lower costs and higher efficiency.
